A four-shot fashion fight in one space, hard cuts, two people only, unarmed, no blood, nobody looks at the lens, every shot has movement in the camera or in the bodies. SHOT 1, wide symmetrical, camera locked at floor level: the two women stand at opposite ends of the light shaft facing each other across the beam, the ivory suit bright on one side and the black leather a silhouette on the other; the first closes her fist, the second settles her weight onto the back foot; dust drifts through the beam and is the only thing that moves. SHOT 2, hard cut to a side tracking shot: the first lunges through the beam and the second pivots, forearms meeting with a hard block, the wide silk sleeve and the leather coat snapping outward with the impact; the camera tracks laterally at hip height and whips with the strike, the concrete wall streaking past behind them. SHOT 3, hard cut to an extreme close-up: a black gloved hand catching an ivory wrist, the silk torqueing and pulling tight, hair strands flying across the backlit dust, both shoulders shaking with effort, only hands and forearms in frame. SHOT 4, hard cut to a low wide: they break apart, one boot skidding across the terrazzo, the second landing in a low crouch, both silhouetted against the arched window with the light shaft between them; the camera tilts up slowly and holds as the dust settles. Cinematic high-fashion campaign, hard contrast between the warm shaft and the cold shadow, motion blur only on the strikes. Sound: skin and cloth impact, a skid of a boot on stone, short breath, the coat settling, an empty concrete room tone.

- [kling4_duel_black_leather.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Comfy-Org/workflow_templates/refs/heads/main/input/kling4_duel_black_leather.png) — second character card
- [kling4_r2v_brutalist_atrium.png](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Comfy-Org/workflow_templates/refs/heads/main/input/kling4_r2v_brutalist_atrium.png) — the space both of them stay inside

## Two characters in one space

Two people in one shot is the hardest thing to keep straight, because the model would rather average them into one face than hold two identities. Treat each reference as a character card: nail the invariants one by one (`keep her pale freckled skin, ash-blonde crop, the scar through her left eyebrow, and her ivory raw-silk suit … exactly as they are`) instead of writing "two women". Contrast the silhouettes on purpose — one bright and one dark, one tailored and one leather — so the audience and the model both keep track of who is where.

Stage it as a fight rather than a pose. Four shots that work in five seconds:

1. wide and symmetrical, both at opposite ends of the light, only the dust moving;
2. side tracking as the first crosses the beam and the block lands, the sleeves snapping outward;
3. extreme close-up on the contact — a gloved hand catching a wrist, fabric torqueing, no faces;
4. low wide as they break apart, silhouetted against the window, the dust settling.

Say `two people only, unarmed, no blood, nobody looks at the lens` and give the camera one behaviour per shot. The third shot is what makes it read as a fight: hands, not faces.
